subject: OpenMSD status: sources landed, join-key quality risk
body:
Hi Bruno, Dmitri,

Status. Raw sources landed April 9: full COCI CSV set and the CrossRef torrent both validated against checksums. The decode path chews through the json.gz shards at about 40 GB/hour on our batch allocation, so the full CrossRef pass is a ~5 hour job, fine.

The risk is join quality, not throughput. DOI normalization mismatches between OpenCitations and CrossRef (case differences, trailing punctuation, a small population of malformed DOIs) mean a naive join drops about 3.8% of citation edges. Worse, the loss isn't uniform - non-English venues are overrepresented in the dropped set, which directly undercuts the "multilingual" pitch. Gustavo's QA sample confirms the skew.

Fix: a normalization + fuzzy-recovery layer before the join, ~2 weeks of my time. That pushes relation extraction from May 8 to around May 15 but recovers an estimated 80% of the dropped edges. I think its clearly worth it - flagging since it eats the milestone buffer.

Rosa
